Tosafot on Kiddushin 65b:11:2.hebrew: ותנא תונא והלה אומר לא אכלתי - הא דנקט "לא אכלתי", ה"ה אם אמר "איני יודע" דפטור, משום דכתיב (שם) "או הודע". והא דנקט "לא אכלתי" — משום דבעי למיתני סיפא גבי "שנים אומרים אכלת חלב והוא אומר לא אכלתי"; ובהא איכא רבותא לר"מ, דאפילו אמר "לא אכלתי" מחייב ר"מ:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 65b:11:2.english: "And the tanna also taught: 'And that [person] says: I did not eat'" - The fact that [the mishna] formulated [it as] "I did not eat," the same law applies if he said "I do not know," that he is exempt, because it is written: "Or if [his sin] be made known to him" (ibid., Leviticus 4:23). And the fact that [the mishna] formulated [it as] "I did not eat" is because it needed to teach the closing clause regarding [a case where] "Two [witnesses] say: 'You ate forbidden fat,' and he says: 'I did not eat'"; and in this [case], there is a novelty according to Rabbi Meir, that even [if] he said "I did not eat," Rabbi Meir holds [him] liable.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 65b:12:1.hebrew: נטמאו טהרותיך והלה שותק נאמן - שאמר לו העד: "בפניך נטמאו". וכן צריך לפרש ב"אכלת חלב", כדפרישית. וקשה, דהא בפ' הנזקין (גיטין דף נד:) מייתי: "היה עושה עמו בטהרות ואמר לו ׳נטמאו טהרותיך׳ — נאמן; ׳טהרות שעשיתי עמך ביום פלוני נטמאו׳ — אינו נאמן". ופריך התם: מאי שנא רישא ומאי שנא סיפא? ומשני: אמר אביי, "כל שבידו — נאמן, וכל שאינו בידו — אינו נאמן; וסיפא איירי שאין הטהרות בידו, לכך אינו נאמן". והיכי אמר אביי דנאמן כשאמר לו "אכלת חלב", ואע"ג שאין בידו להאכילו חלב?! וכן קשה לקמן, דנאמן לומר "שורך נרבע", אע"ג דאין בידו להרביע שורו! וי"ל, דההיא דהנזקין מיירי כשאינו שותק, אלא מכחישו; והכא איירי כששותק, ואינו מכחישו. ומיהו קשה מרבא, דהכא משמע דלא פליג רבא עליה דאביי, דאמר דכל דבר שאין בידו בעי שותק; והתם קאמר רבא: "אשכחיה ולא אמר ליה, והדר אשכחיה ואמר ליה — אינו נאמן", משמע: אבל אי אמר ליה מיד — נאמן בכל ענין, אפי' אין בידו ואפי' אין שותק, והכא לא פליג אאביי דבאין בידו בעי שותק! וי"ל: שאני התם, לפי שהיה בידו פעם אחת, דהיינו בשעת שעשאו; אבל הכא, מעולם לא היה בידו כלל, ולכן בעי שותק. ונראה דהלכה כרבא לגבי אביי. ועתה בענין זה יש שלשה דינים: בדבר שהיה בידו, כגון ההיא ד"היה עושה עמו בטהרות" — נאמן, ואפי' לא היה שותק; ובדבר שאין בידו לעולם, כגון "אכלת חלב" ו"שורך נרבע" — אי שתיק מהימן, ואי לא שתיק לא מהימן; ובדבר שאין בידו עתה אבל היה בידו פעם אחרת — בהא פליגי אביי ורבא, כדפירשתי התם גבי "טהרות שעשיתי עמך", דלרבא היכא דאשכחיה ואמר ליה מהימן, ואפילו אינו שותק; והלכה כרבא כדפרישית. ושותק דאמר בשמעתין דנאמן, נראה לר"י דהיינו בדבר שיש לו לידע, כגון שאמר לו: "נתנסך יינך בפניך", דומיא ד"אכלת חלב"; אבל אם אמר לו: "נתנסך יינך שלא בפניך" ושותק — ההיא שתיקה אינה כהודאה, שלכך לא ישיב לו, לפי שלא היה יודע בירור הדבר. ומה שאמרנו דבר שאינו בידו כי אינו שותק לא מהימן — היינו גברא דלא מהימן כבי תרי; אבל אי מהימן ליה כבי תרי — נאמן, כדאמר בסמוך גבי סמיא, דקאמר רבא דנאמן, אע"ג דהוי דבר שבערוה ואין דבר שבערוה פחות משנים, כל שכן דנאמן במילתא אחריתי. וצריך לומר דהא דאמר בכל דוכתין (גיטין דף ב:) "עד אחד נאמן באיסורין" — היינו דוקא להתיר, כגון "בשר זו מנוקרת" או "חתיכה זו של שומן", אבל לאסור הדבר אינו נאמן, אלא כמו שפירשתי. והא דאמרינן דבדבר שאינו בידו כי אינו שותק לא מהימן — היינו דוקא בדבר שאינו יכול להתברר; אבל בדבר שיכול להתברר, כגון שאמר לו: "יש שרץ בטהרותיך" או "עובד כוכבים מנסך יינך, בא ואראך האיסור" — בהא ודאי יש לחוש לדבריו ולבדוק, כדאמר לקמן (עמוד ב) גבי בעל מום, דמצי אמר ליה "שלח ואחוי". וכשאדם עושה חבירו שליח לשמור יינו או להביא מן המרתף — נאמן, דהיינו בידו, ומהימן עליה כבי תרי כשסומך עליו; והא דבעינן שותק — היינו דוקא דלא עשאו שליח:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 65b:12:1.english: "Your ritually pure items were defiled," and that one is silent, he is believed - Meaning that the witness said to him: "They were defiled in your presence." And one must likewise explain [the earlier case of] "You ate forbidden fat," as I have explained. And this is difficult: for in the chapter [entitled] HaNizakin (Gittin 54b), [the Gemara] cites: "If one was preparing ritually pure items with him and said to him: 'Your ritually pure items were defiled,' he is believed; [if he said:] 'The ritually pure items that I prepared with you on such-and-such a day were defiled,' he is not believed." And [the Gemara] challenges there: What is the difference between the first clause and the latter clause? And it answers: Abaye said, "Whoever has the matter in his power is believed, and whoever does not have the matter in his power is not believed; and the latter clause deals with [a case where] the ritually pure items are no longer in his power, which is why he is not believed." And how could Abaye say [here] that he is believed when he said to him: "You ate forbidden fat," even though it is not in his power to feed him forbidden fat?! And so too it is difficult regarding what is stated later (66a), that [a single witness] is believed to say: "Your ox was used for bestiality," even though it is not in his power to have his ox used for bestiality! And one can say that that [baraita cited in] HaNizakin deals with [a case where] he is not silent, but rather contradicts him; whereas here it deals with [a case where] he is silent and does not contradict him. However, there is a difficulty from Rava: for here it implies that Rava does not disagree with Abaye, who says that for anything that is not in his power, he requires [the owner to be] silent; yet there [in Gittin 54b] Rava says: "If he met him and did not tell him, and then met him again and told him, he is not believed" — which implies: but if he told him immediately, he is believed in any case, even if it is not in his power and even if he is not silent! Yet here he does not disagree with Abaye that when it is not in his power, he requires [the owner to be] silent! And one can say: It is different there, because it was in his power once, namely at the time that he prepared them; but here, it was never in his power at all, and therefore it requires [him to be] silent. And it appears that the halakhah follows Rava against Abaye. And now, in this matter, there are three rules: In a matter that was in his power, such as that [case] where he was preparing ritually pure items with him, he is believed, even if [the owner] was not silent; and in a matter that is never in his power, such as "You ate forbidden fat" and "Your ox was used for bestiality," if he is silent he is believed, and if he is not silent he is not believed; and in a matter that is not in his power now, but was in his power at another time — regarding this Abaye and Rava disagree, as I explained there concerning "the ritually pure items that I prepared with you," for according to Rava, where he met him and told him [immediately] he is believed, and even if he is not silent; and the halakhah follows Rava, as I have explained. And as for the silent one regarding whom it is said in our sugya that [the witness] is believed — it appears to the Ri that this is specifically in a matter that he ought to know, such as where he said to him: "Your wine was poured as a libation in your presence," similar to "You ate forbidden fat"; but if he said to him: "Your wine was poured as a libation not in your presence" and he is silent, that silence is not [considered] like an admission, for that is why he does not answer him, because he did not know the facts of the matter clearly. And that which we said, that in a matter that is not in his power, when he is not silent, he is not believed — this applies [only to an ordinary] person who is not believed like two [witnesses]; but if he is believed by him like two [witnesses], he is believed, as [the Gemara] says nearby regarding the blind man (66a), where Rava says that he is believed even though it is a matter of forbidden sexual relations, and no matter of forbidden sexual relations [can be established by] fewer than two [witnesses] — all the more so that he is believed in any other matter! And one must say that that which [the Gemara] states everywhere (Gittin 2b) that "one witness is believed in [matters of ritual] prohibitions" — that is specifically to permit [an item], such as [attesting that] "this meat is porged" or "this piece is [permitted] fat"; but to forbid the item he is not believed, except as I have explained. And that which we said, that in a matter that is not in his power, when he is not silent, he is not believed — that is specifically in a matter that cannot be verified; but in a matter that can be verified, such as where he said to him: "There is a creeping animal in your ritually pure items," or "An idolater is pouring your wine as a libation, come and I will show you the forbidden act" — in this [case] one certainly must suspect his words and investigate, as [the Gemara] says later (66b) regarding a blemished [priest], where he can say to him: "Strip and show [me]." And when a person appoints his fellow as an agent to guard his wine or to bring [it] from the cellar, he is believed, for that is in his power and he is believed by him like two [witnesses] when he relies upon him. And that which we require [the owner to be] silent — that is specifically where he did not appoint him an agent.
